text:
Sanjay Patel: thinking out loud — what if instead of hard-dipping into the token pool on big short spikes we apply an "excess-filter" layer that smooths only the delta above a short-window baseline?
Maria Chen: curious, sketch the user-visible behaviour. is this a drop-or-delay approach?
Sanjay Patel: delay-first. small extra requests get tiny randomized delays (10-200ms) to allow batching + refill to absorb them; huge surges fall back to existing rejection path. idea is to keep steady-state unaffected but avoid catastrophic token drain on short blips.
Kevin O'Neill: that jittered delay + small queue sounds nice. does it change billing semantics?
Sanjay Patel: no change in billing. tokens consumed when served; excess-filter only defers/queues a tiny fraction to protect shared pool. metric-wise we should surface 'excess_delays' and 'excess_rejections' per org/key.
Jia Li: config sketch — something like:
```json
{
  "excess_filter": {
    "window_seconds": 6,
    "baseline_percentile": 50,
    "soft_threshold_multiplier": 2.5,
    "max_delay_ms": 200,
    "max_queue_depth": 8
  }
}
```
Sanjay Patel: exactly. baseline via short rolling percentile (50th of last 6s). soft threshold = baseline * multiplier. only excess over that goes through filter.
Maria Chen: how do we avoid thundering queues where many clients get queued and then all drain at once? need per-key randomized backoff and token-aware dequeue rate.
Kevin O'Neill: randomized pop + token-aware dequeue is doable. propose a token-aware leaky dequeue that scales to available token refill rate: dequeue_rate = min(max_queue_depth, refill_rate * alpha).
Jia Li: for telemetry, we should add a new per-org timeseries: excess_score (0-1), queued_requests, avg_excess_delay_ms, pct_excess_reject. Also add alert if queued_requests / org_capacity > 0.3 for > 1m.
Sanjay Patel: console UX idea: show a small "Transient protection" line on the quota card with a sparkline and a hover explaining the soft-throttle window. allow customer to opt-out (advanced) or tune multiplier.
Maria Chen: opt-out might be risky for SRE customers who rely on guarantees. make it default-on for hosted, default-off for Dedicated/Private, and require explicit consent in Private (doc + checkbox).
Kevin O'Neill: rollout plan: feature flag in rate-limiter service + expose a config in org-provisioning. Canary 2% of live requests for 48h -> 10% for a day -> ramp. Collect p95/p99 latencies, rejection rate delta, queued requests, and any user error reports.
rate-limit-bot: deploy triggered: feature-toggle "excess-filter-v1" created by sanjay.p at 2055000030
Jia Li: probes to run during canary: generate synthetic short spikes (burst 200 rps for 8s) and steady-state load (20 rps). expected: 200 spike should see +queued_requests but <1% extra rejections, steady load unchanged.
Maria Chen: also test fairness across keys in same org: one noisy key should not eat credits for others. run mixed-key scenarios.
Sanjay Patel: right — we'll implement per-key filtering + org-level guard to prevent per-key bypass by spinning up many keys. per-key queue cap + org admission controller.
Kevin O'Neill: one implementation caveat: this filter touches the hot path. keep minimal allocations. prefer ring buffer per token-bucket shard, not per-request heap allocations.
Jia Li: I'll prototype in sandbox-rate-limiter branch. will add metrics and a small UI flag in console-dev.
Sanjay Patel: thanks — let's keep messages short in the PR and include the config json and test harness. tagging @Maria for UX decisions. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: noted. will draft hover text and opt-out flow.
rate-limit-bot: canary monitor created: excess-filter-v1-monitor (checks: p99 latency, rejection-rate, queued_requests)
Kevin O'Neill: tiny note — add chaos scenario where the delayed queue consumer dies; ensure we have safe fallback to immediate rejection to avoid unbounded queue growth.
Sanjay Patel: good call. add a max_queue_age_ms and fallback-reject boolean. default fallback true.
Jia Li: putting up draft PR later today with perf tests.
Maria Chen: thanks team, excited to see if this reduces noisy neighbor hits without hurting latency for normal users.
